content_voiceover: This table breaks down mutation frequencies across the MDS/MPN overlap syndromes, chronic myelomonocytic leukemia, atypical CML, MDS/MPN with ring sideroblasts and thrombocytosis, and MDS/MPN unclassifiable, organized by functional gene class. A few patterns are worth memorizing. TET2, DNMT3A, and ASXL1, the epigenetic class three genes, dominate CMML, each mutated in a third to over half of cases. Atypical CML stands out for its high rate of SETBP1 and ASXL1 mutations, along with frequent splicing gene involvement, particularly SRSF2. RARS-T, now folded into MDS/MPN with ring sideroblasts and thrombocytosis, is defined by its striking splicing mutation burden, especially ZRSR2 at eighty percent and SF3B1, reflecting its close relationship to ring sideroblast morphology. MDS/MPN unclassifiable shows a more mixed signature with relatively higher RUNX1 involvement. Recognizing which gene class dominates which entity helps you triangulate the diagnosis on a board vignette even before the full clinical picture is spelled out.
keypoints: CMML is driven by TET2, DNMT3A, ASXL1 epigenetic mutations
Atypical CML enriched for SETBP1 and ASXL1
RARS-T defined by high splicing mutation burden, especially ZRSR2 and SF3B1
MDS/MPN-U shows relatively higher RUNX1 involvement
keypoint_voiceover: For boards, anchor each MDS/MPN overlap entity to its signature mutation class. CMML pairs with TET2, DNMT3A, and ASXL1. Atypical CML pairs with SETBP1 and ASXL1. RARS-T pairs with splicing mutations, ZRSR2 and SF3B1 especially. And MDS/MPN unclassifiable tends to show more RUNX1 involvement than the others.
